name: rag_sql_query
description:
Query structured data in PostgreSQL database using SQL.

When to use (not exhaustive):
- Querying structured data with well-defined schemas
- Performing exact lookups, filters, aggregations, or joins
- Need precise, deterministic results based on structured criteria

Rules:
- NEVER select all columns, return only the fields relevant to the step you are performing
- Use only existing column names and respect which column belongs to which table
- Do not invent tables or columns
- For keyword searches, use strict equality only if the question demands exact matches or trivial, else:
    - Use % for trigram matching operator (pg_trgm)
    - Use dmetaphone for phonetic search (fuzzystrmatch)
- Qualify column names with table names when needed

Returns:
An object with two fields:
- items: result entries (empty when no rows match), each with:
    - title: source title, if available
    - row: the selected columns and their values
    - source_type: source data identifier
    - url: link to the source, if available
- message: a note about the result (e.g. when no rows match or results were truncated)

sql.description: Syntactically valid SQL query for PostgreSQL

db_name.description: Name of the PostgreSQL database to query

name: rag_vector_query
description:
Search unstructured text data using semantic similarity in the Qdrant vector database.

When to use (not exhaustive):
- Searching within unstructured text fields (descriptions, abstracts, content, etc.)
- Finding conceptually similar or related information
- When you need semantic understanding rather than exact matches

Tips:
- You can rewrite the original to be more search-friendly if needed
- Longer, descriptive, and more detailed queries produce better results than short keywords

Filter format follows Qdrant's native filter JSON. Top-level keys combine clauses:
- must: AND (all clauses must match)
- should: OR (at least one clause must match)
- must_not: NOT (no clause may match)

Each clause is one of these shapes (replace <field> with the payload key name):
- equality: {"key": "<field>", "match": {"value": "x"}}
- in list: {"key": "<field>", "match": {"any": ["x", "y"]}}
- not in list: {"key": "<field>", "match": {"except": ["x", "y"]}}
- full-text: {"key": "<field>", "match": {"text": "x"}} (requires text index)
- range: {"key": "<field>", "range": {"gt": 1, "gte": 1, "lt": 10, "lte": 10}}
- is empty: {"is_empty": {"key": "<field>"}}
- is null: {"is_null": {"key": "<field>"}}

Examples:
- Single equality:
  {"must": [{"key": "source_type", "match": {"value": "pubmed"}}]}
- AND with range:
  {"must": [{"key": "source_type", "match": {"value": "pubmed"}}, {"key": "year", "range": {"gte": 2020}}]}
- OR of two values:
  {"should": [{"key": "source_type", "match": {"value": "pubmed"}}, {"key": "source_type", "match": {"value": "dailymed"}}]}
- Nested (match A AND (B OR C)):
  {"must": [{"key": "source_type", "match": {"value": "pubmed"}}, {"should": [{"key": "year", "range": {"gte": 2023}}, {"key": "mesh_terms", "match": {"any": ["oncology"]}}]}]}

Returns:
An object with two fields:
- items: result entries (empty when nothing matches), each with:
    - title: source title, if available
    - content: the matched text
    - source_type: source data identifier
    - relevance_score: similarity or reranker score
    - url: link to the source, if available
- message: a note about the result if applicable, otherwise empty string

query.description: Natural language query string to search for

collection_name.description: Name of the Qdrant collection to query

filters.description: Metadata filter. See docstring for examples.

top_k.description: Number of top similar results to return

name: adr_retrieve_drug_info
description:
Look up a drug's official labeling sections in the configured drug-label databases (currently DailyMed).

Takes an **English brand or generic (INN) name**. Korean drug names will NOT match the label
data -- resolve them to their English ingredient name first (e.g. with `openapi_mfds_get_drug_indication`,
whose `ingredient_eng` is the English INN) and pass that name here.

Returns a `ListResult` of citable `DrugLabelResult` items -- one per labeling section, covering
warnings/precautions, adverse reactions and drug interactions -- each carrying the section text
and a link to the source label. `message` reports, per source, how many sections were found and
which of three things went wrong when nothing came back: the source was unavailable, the name
matched no product, or the product carries no configured label sections.

name: index_list_documents
description:
List documents in the corpus to anchor retrieval, ranked by semantic similarity to `query` when given. Paginated via `limit` and `offset`.

Returns:
- results: list of documents, each with:
  - node_id: document root node id. Used for other tools that requires top-level document node id, i.e. doc_id.
  - title
  - summary
  - total_pages
  - score: similarity in [0, 1], omitted if query is null.
- total_results: total available documents.
- offset: offset applied.
- message: remaining-results guidance. May be omitted.

corpus_tag.description: The document corpus to query. Available: 'hira', 'guideline'.

query.description: Optional search query to rank documents by semantic similarity to their summary.

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return.

offset.description: Number of top-ranked documents to skip, to page past the first page of results.

name: index_get_document_structure
description:
Return the structure of the document, represented as tree, relative to `node_id`, expanded `depth` levels.
At most 50 nodes are returned per call.

Each node carries:
- node_id: id to use when re-anchoring a follow-up call here.
- title: section heading.
- summary: content summary.
- range: [start_page, end_page] covered by this node. Use it to pass to `get_page_content` later.
- max_descendant_depth: max depth below this node (0 = leaf).
- children: List of direct child nodes. Only present when this node is expanded.
- total_descendant: Total descendants below it. Only present when this node is NOT expanded (depth boundary or leaf).

Returns:
- structure: serialized subtree (recursively nested dicts).
- message: explanation of any clamping/truncation. May be omitted.

corpus_tag.description: The document corpus to query. Available: 'hira', 'guideline'.

node_id.description: The node id to anchor on.

depth.description: Expansion depth relative to node with node_id. 0 = anchor only, 1 = anchor + immediate children, N = N levels of descendants.

name: index_get_relevant_nodes
description:
Retrieve top-K semantically similar nodes based on the node summary with respect to the query.
The semantic search is ONLY performed against LEAF nodes.

Returns:
List of dictionaries, each containing:
- node_id
- title: node section heading
- summary: the summary content of this node.
- range: [start_page, end_page] covered by this node. Use it to pass to `get_page_content` later.
- doc_id: root node_id of the document this node belongs to.
- doc_title: full title of that document.
- ancestors: list of {node_id, title} of this node's ancestor from the doc root node. Can be used to traverse upwards
- score: cosine similarity in [0, 1], higher is more similar.

corpus_tag.description: The document corpus to query. Available: 'hira', 'guideline'.

query.description: Natural language query string. Longer, more descriptive queries produce better results than short keywords.

node_id.description: If set, confine the search to this node and every descendant under it. Use null to search across all documents in the corpus.

k.description: Maximum number of top similar nodes to return.

name: index_keyword_search
description:
Lexical keyword search over raw page text, for exact terms.
Hits are ranked by distinct terms matched then total occurrences, paginated via `limit` and `offset`.

Returns:
- results: list of page hits (at most `limit`), each with:
  - doc_id: root node_id of the document.
  - doc_title: document title.
  - node_id: first leaf covering this page, or null on a coverage gap. Pass the parent node_id to `get_document_structure` to get broader context.
  - summary: that leaf's summary, for context. Empty when node_id is null.
  - page: 1-indexed page number within the document (doc_id). Pass to `get_page_content` for the full page.
  - snippet: matched text in the text within the page, matches wrapped in **.
  - match_count: total term occurrences on the page.
  - matched_terms: query terms found on the page.
- total_results: total matching pages before pagination.
- offset: offset applied to this response.
- message: remaining-results or no-match guidance. May be omitted.

corpus_tag.description: The document corpus to query. Available: 'hira', 'guideline'.

query.description: Keyword to match exactly (case-insensitive) in raw page text. Separate with comma to enter multiple keywords.

doc_id.description: Top-level document (root) node id, as returned by `list_documents`. Null searches all documents in the corpus.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return.

offset.description: Number of top-ranked hits to skip, to fetch the remaining results when total match exceeds limit.

name: index_get_page_content
description:
Fetch raw text for a contiguous page range of a document.

Page numbers are 1-indexed and both `start_page` and `end_page` are
inclusive. At most 20 pages are returned per call.

Returns:
- title: the document's title.
- pages: list of {"page": int, "text": str}. Pages that contain a flowchart/diagram also have
  "charts": a list of {"block": int, "paths": [str]}. Each entry is one flowchart on the page.
  "paths" lists every route through the flowchart from start to end, written as plain text
  with steps joined by " → " and branch conditions as " →(condition)→ ".
  "block" is the position of the text block the chart was extracted from within the page.
- source_type: source data identifier.
- url: link to the source, if available.
- message: explanation of any clamping/truncation. Empty when none.

corpus_tag.description: The document corpus to query. Available: 'hira', 'guideline'.

doc_id.description: Top-level document node id, as returned by `list_documents`. Must be the top-level (root) node id of a document.

outputSchema.description:
Contiguous page range of an index document. Each page dict holds `page` (1-indexed) and
`text`, plus `charts` (list of `{block, paths}` flowchart dicts) on pages that carry one.

name: openapi_mfds_get_drug_indication
description:
Get a Korean drug's MFDS(식약처) 효능·효과(허가 적응증) + ATC code, and optionally 용법용량.

Use this to judge whether a 처방 상병 is within the drug's APPROVED indication (허가 적응증) — the
check `openapi_mfds_check_drug_permission` cannot answer (that one gives 허가 여부/상태 only). Each returned item
carries `indication` (효능효과, the 허가 적응증 목록) and `notice`, the 사용상의 주의사항 절 named by
`notice_clause` (기본 금기): 금기 상병에 투여한 건은 허가 적응증 안이어도 삭감 대상이므로 적응증과 함께
대조하라. Many
products (esp. 항암제) carry the full 효능효과 text; for some older/generic items the text is not
machine-readable and only a 허가 PDF link (`doc_url`) is returned — in that case fall back to the HIRA
급여기준 for the 적응증. 용법용량 comes only when `include_dosage` is set; a drug's 허가사항 can run to
tens of thousands of characters per product, so document text is capped per response. Items come
best-match-first and each clipped text says how many characters were dropped and which exact 품명 to
re-query to read that one item in full. Reason: 식약처 detail op getDrugPrdtPrmsnDtlInq06 (same
service/key as permission).

drug_name.description: Korean drug product name; partial match is OK (e.g. '키트루다')

num_rows.description: Max number of matching products to return

include_dosage.description: Also return 용법용량. Off by default: it is several times the size of 효능효과 and it settles only the 허가 축 — 급여의 정량 인정조건은 HIRA 고시 소관이다. Turn it ON when 용법용량 is what is ASKED FOR or what DECIDES the case: (1) the question asks for the 허가사항 itself (효능효과·용법용량·금기 확인 요청) — then it is the requested output, not a nice-to-have, and no other source has it; (2) 투여 용량·투여기간·투여주기가 허가 범위를 넘었는지, (3) 신기능·간기능·체중·연령 때문에 용량을 조정해야 하는지가 쟁점일 때(용법용량은 CrCl 구간별 용량표를 담는다 — 세피데로콜 CrCl<15 → 0.75g q12h), (4) 급여기준이 '허가사항 범위 내 투여'를 조건으로 걸고 그 준수 여부를 묻는 경우. 고시는 '투여기간 며칠 이내' 같은 인정조건을 담지만 약제별 mg/CrCl 용량표는 담지 않으므로(실측), 그 값은 여기서만 나온다. Do NOT turn it on just because the question PRINTS a number: 처방 기술의 용량('alendronate 70mg 주 1회 투여 중'), 검사수치(mg/dL·IU/mL·U/L), 재료·행위 개수는 용법용량과 무관하다 — 실측 30문항 중 8문항이 용량성 수치를 담았고 용법용량이 필요한 문항은 0이었다.

notice_clause.description: 사용상의 주의사항에서 함께 가져올 절의 제목 일부. 기본값 '투여하지 말'은 금기(다음 환자에는 투여하지 말 것)를 집어온다 — 금기 상병에 투여한 건은 허가 적응증 안이어도 삭감 대상이다. 다른 절이 쟁점이면 그 절의 제목 일부를 그대로 넘겨라: '상호작용'(병용), '임부', '소아', '고령자', '신장애', '경고'. 빈 문자열이면 아무 절도 담지 않는다.

description:
Look a drug up in the HIRA 약제급여목록표 (약가기준정보) to decide 급여 등재 여부 and get its
상한금액 · 약가코드 · 적용시작일.

This is the 급여 counterpart to the MFDS 허가 tools, and the two can disagree — a product may be
MFDS-정상(허가 유효) while `pay_type` here is '삭제'(급여목록에서 삭제), which is the
허가내비급여/전액본인부담 case and NOT 허가초과. Per row: `pay_type` (급여/삭제), `max_price`
(상한금액, 원), `drug_code` (mdsCd — the 약가코드 written on the 명세서), `ingredient_code`

name: openapi_law_search
description:
Find a Korean 법령 by name and get its MST — the handle the other law tools take.

Search matches the 법령명 ONLY; there is NO full-text search over 조문, so search by the name of a
law, not by the rule you are looking for. Partial names work and are the point: '감염병' returns
the 법률 + 시행령 + 시행규칙 together, and common 약칭 resolve ('감염병예방법' → '감염병의 예방 및
관리에 관한 법률').

If you are not certain of the 법령명, search a BROAD topic word and pick from the list. Do NOT
assert a 법령명 or 조문번호 from memory — laws are enacted and renamed (간호법, 2024) and a
confident wrong guess retrieves the wrong statute.

A 법령 has three tiers that answer different questions: 법률 (the rule), 대통령령/시행령 (요건·범위),
부령/시행규칙 (서식·절차·기한). Look at all three tiers before concluding.

`kind='law'` rows can be opened with openapi_law_list_articles / openapi_law_get_article; 행정규칙 and 자치법규 are
not served as 조문 and this tool can only point at them.

characters for the 법률 alone.

name: openapi_law_get_article
description:
Fetch the full text of specific 조문 — the citable law tool. Answer from these, never from memory.

Each item carries `article_label` (제41조의2), `article_title`, `content` (조문제목 + every 항·호·목
with its <개정 2016.2.3> markers), `effective_date` (조문시행일자 — a 조문 can be in force on a date
the 법령 as a whole is not), and a law.go.kr permalink. Cite `law_name article_label(제목)`.

`article_keys` are 조문키 from openapi_law_list_articles. Ask for every 조문 you need in ONE call
rather than one call per 조문, up to 20 — these are ENFORCED ceilings, not advice: past 20 조문, or
past the call's character budget, the extra keys are refused and named back to you so you can ask
again. Refused is not absent, and a key that is not in this 법령 at all is reported separately.

an earlier date (`efYd` is accepted and ignored). So when the question is pinned to a date — a
진료일자, a 신고 기한, "그때는 어땠나" — compare that date against `effective_date`: if the 조문 took
effect AFTER it, this text is NOT the rule that applied, and you must say so instead of answering
from it. A 삭제된 조문 stays in the 목차 and returns "제N조 삭제 <date>", which is itself the answer.
